From: Tom Avery <tom.avery@blueline.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T18:11:00Z
Subject: Streaming chat endpoint - spike in p99 latency and 502 errors during 18:00-19:00 UTC

Hi Marissa,

We saw a recurring problem last night during our evening peak (18:00-19:00 UTC): the hosted streaming chat endpoint (SSE) experienced a dramatic p99 latency spike from ~480ms to >6.2s and intermittent 502s. Our dashboard shows a simultaneous throughput drop and a lot of aborted client connections. This impacted several active support chats and one customer-facing widget.

Quick stats from our side:
- Window: 2028-07-23 18:03 - 18:47 UTC
- p95: 620ms -> 1.8s (normal ~540ms)
- p99: 480ms -> 6.2s
- 502 count: ~1.2% of requests in window
- Concurrent connections: peaked ~3.6k

We opened a ticket with ops@blueline.com who forwarded some client-side traces attached (logs_20280723_client.txt). Can you confirm whether Redwood saw the same, and what root cause and ETA for mitigation are? This is impacting our SLAs and we're escalating internally.

Thanks,
Tom Avery
Head of Platform Integrations
BlueLine Commerce

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T18:28:00Z
Subject: Escalation: BlueLine - streaming SSE p99 spike + 502s (urgent)

Markus / Jonas —

BlueLine (DL-5821) reporting a severe p99 latency regression and ~1% 502s during evening peak (18:00-19:00 UTC). They report ~3.6k concurrent connections. They are hosted in our us-east region and have been on the hosted streaming API; they haven't changed client config. Sample client traces attached (from customer).

Observed impact per customer: slowed UI responses, abandoned chats, SLA impact. Customer asks for root cause and ETA.

Things I noticed from preliminary dashboard checks:
- Sudden jump in p99 across streaming endpoints in us-east beginning 18:03 UTC, lasted ~44 minutes.
- Error rates (502) correlated with a small set of backend instances (id shard-3*).
- A canary rollout of a quantized variant of v2-chat-opt was pushed to a subset of serving hosts last night at 17:50 UTC (I saw the rollout tag in the deploy logs).

Attachments: logs_20280723_client.txt (from customer), redwood_metrics_1800-1900.csv (brief sample).

Proposed immediate actions (in parallel):
1) SRE: pin BlueLine traffic off shard-3 and failover to standby pools.
2) Infra: roll back the quantized v2-chat-opt variant from the canary hosts that match shard-3.
3) Ops: temporarily increase streaming connection concurrency and enable aggressive connection backpressure to shed malformed clients.
4) Product/AE: offer a one-off credit if we confirm regression source is our rollout.

Please confirm next steps / who will own each action. I can coordinate customer communications.

—Marissa

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T19:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: BlueLine - streaming SSE p99 spike + 502s (urgent)

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the signal. Quick sync from infra/SRE: we've reproduced the p99 spike in our telemetry and narrowed the affected hosts to a subset of the us-east streaming pool (matching shard-3 as you saw). Initial hypothesis: an interaction between the new quantized kernel selection for v2-chat-opt and our batching window heuristics causing KV-cache thrash under high concurrency; that combination can amplify tail latency for streaming sockets and, under queue pressure, produce upstream 502s as requests time out.

Actions taken at 19:06 UTC:
- Scoped and rolled back the quantized candidate on the 8 hosts that map to shard-3 (rollback_patch.diff attached).
- Rebalanced incoming BlueLine connections away from those hosts to the standby pool; connection counts stabilized within ~3 minutes.
- Applied a temporary reduction of batch size for streaming endpoints to lower per-request latency and reduce KV eviction churn.

Immediate result: p99 reduced from ~6.2s to ~820ms in the next sampling window; 502s dropped to ~0.05% across their traffic. We continue to watch.

Planned follow-ups:
- Post-mortem to cover: kernel selection telemetry gaps, canary scope rules, automatic fallback policy for quantized variants.
- Engineering to add a targeted test for high-concurrency SSE loads with quantized kernels in the e2e perf suite.
- Product/legal to review compensation if customer confirms SLA breach.

I'll keep this thread updated; attaching current server-side logs and the rollback diff.

—Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.com
(attachment: rollback_patch.diff)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Avery <tom.avery@blueline.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T23:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat endpoint - spike in p99 latency and 502 errors during 18:00-19:00 UTC

Tom —

Update and apologies for the disruption. Summary: engineering identified an interaction between a canary quantized model rollout and streaming batching heuristics on a small set of us-east hosts (shard-3). We rolled back the candidate and rebalanced connections; you should see normal behavior restored after ~19:10 UTC. Markus' team reduced batch size as a temporary mitigation, and 502s dropped to baseline.

Next steps on our side:
- Full post-mortem and ticket with mitigation timeline (by 2028-07-25).
- Add dedicated canary rules to prevent quantized kernels from landing on streaming-critical shards without additional perf gating.
- We'll propose a goodwill credit for the incident window; I'll follow up with the compensation details tomorrow.

Can you confirm that BlueLine's monitoring shows stabilized metrics? We'll keep the on-call rotation watching through your next evening peak. Again — very sorry for the disruption.

Best,
Marissa Cole
